definition.text: Reason while listening, then save and reuse the results when a user asks a question.

items.text: Keep 20 reviewed questions across six meetings, with answer facts and six clips of ordinary discussion.
Generate or revise and validate reference answers for all 105 questions.
Preserve the question recordings and keep evaluation speakers separate from earlier voice-tuning speakers.
Collect independent listening ratings before making stronger claims about voice quality and naturalness.
Compare full transcripts, recent speech, transcripts without speaker labels and automatic notes.
Review task owners, changed decisions, missing facts and unreliable earlier reasoning outputs.
The first note system loses useful facts and is not ready for speech tests.
Define the experiment families, notation and amortized-thinking terminology.
Implement shared S1 answer extraction, scoring and token accounting.
items.evidence: Evaluator v0.1.2 passes 46 CPU checks; original 43-check snapshot and three historical examples are retained separately.

items.text: Implement run-time progress updates from the same saved records as the checklists.

items.text: Check evaluator behavior on saved real outputs and labeled failure fixtures.
items.evidence: Three earlier real outputs and 43 CPU checks pass.

items.text: Run and inspect a small end-to-end DuplexOmni S1 pilot, including an early and a later request.
items.evidence: Three real meeting requests tested on one A100 80 GB; raw outputs, recorded speech and source facts reviewed. Full protocol remains unvalidated.

items.text: Publish an actual pilot output with its request, answer facts, score and explanation.
items.evidence: Actual input excerpts, S1 response audio, source facts, raw text and score explanations are published together.

items.text: Diagnose and repair empty or unusable S1 responses before full evaluation.
items.evidence: Matched caller reproduces all 40 short-example response records; all 41 pressure contexts produce speech, but question recognition is unstable and 0/11 eligible answers are complete within the recorded window.

items.text: Run both listening methods and inspect their meeting answers against source facts.
items.evidence: Two native listening methods: 4/4 meeting outputs saved and 4/4 source reviews recorded; full protocol remains unvalidated. Neither method gives a complete meeting answer; recognition remains unresolved.

items.text: Reproduce the working DailyTalk recipe and compare it with the current S1 runner.
items.evidence: The original helper and new native runner match all 40 response-field records; their spoken discount/full-price answers agree. P01 request-only recognition passes (WER 0.063), while its folder-status answer is unsupported without earlier evidence.

items.text: Test P01 with request-only audio and every sentence-based increase in earlier context.
items.evidence: 41/41 contexts reviewed for one question; 20 preserve question meaning in ASR, and 0/11 eligible contexts give complete reference answers within 19.2 s.

items.text: Compare microphone signals across all 41 histories and inspect actual spoken-response content.
items.evidence: Three signals at 41 lengths: 78 new native replays, 3 generation failures shown as gaps, 33 eligible spoken answers scored by a qualified local judge and audited against the source; 0 complete. One question; full protocol remains unvalidated.

items.text: Qualify native S1 history and automatic judging, then freeze the evaluation protocol before broader experiments.
items.evidence: The one-question microphone sweep is reviewed and the revised local judge passed twelve authored checks; validate all 105 references, qualify judging on distinct questions and check the other S1 callers before full-bank evaluation.

stages.title: 4. Add tools and learn when to act

items.text: Add one document lookup with known results and a case where later speech changes the request.
Compare simple rules for listening, amortized thinking, answering, asking, using a tool and cancelling work.
Train an action policy only after the rules and scoring are reliable.
